# firstboot_load_balancer (Resource)

A load balancer that spreads traffic across servers.

**It reaches its backends over a PRIVATE network, which is why `network_id` is required and why every backend must already be a member of it.** Public addresses are not reachable from here: tenant isolation flags each guest's public bridge port. Joining a network needs a restart the customer schedules, so a server has to be on the network before it can be a backend -- put `network_id` on the `firstboot_server` too, and Terraform's dependency graph does the rest.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Hostname format: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. The API has no rename, so a change replaces the load balancer, which means a NEW public address.
- `network_id` (String) The private network the load balancer reaches its backends over. It cannot be moved to another network, so a change replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `algorithm` (String) `round_robin` (the default) or `least_connections`. Applied in place, together with the rules and the health check.
- `backend_ids` (List of String) Servers behind the load balancer, each already a member of `network_id`. Replaced as a whole set, in place.
- `health_check` (Attributes) How a backend is judged healthy. Omit it for a TCP check every 10 seconds, which is what the platform applies. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--health_check))
- `plan` (String) `lb-1`, `lb-2` or `lb-3`; defaults to `lb-1`.

**There is no resize.** A plan change replaces the load balancer and its address with it, which is why this forces replacement rather than pretending to apply in place.
- `project_id` (String) Optional project to group the load balancer under. Changing it moves the load balancer in place; it is not a replacement.
- `region` (String) Region slug; defaults to the platform's first active region. It has to be the network's region, and it cannot be changed afterwards.
- `restrict_backends` (Boolean) Close each backend's target port to everything except this load balancer. Default `true`, and worth leaving on: without it the backends stay reachable directly and the load balancer is a suggestion rather than a door.

**Write-only.** The API does not return it, so a change here cannot be detected and cannot be applied; it forces replacement instead of promising something the apply would not do.
- `rule` (Block List) One forwarding rule. The whole set is replaced on every change. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags on this load balancer, used to select it from a `firstboot_*` data source and to filter it in the panel.

At most 10, each up to 32 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `:` and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit. `env:prod` is a convention, not a schema: a tag is one flat string.

**Written exactly as given.** The API stores tags lowercased, so a tag that is not already lowercase is refused at plan time rather than silently rewritten — a rewritten value would differ from the configuration on every subsequent plan.
- `wait_for_ready` (Boolean) Whether apply waits for the load balancer to finish provisioning.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `healthy_count` (Number) How many backends passed their last probe. Zero on a load balancer that was just created: the first probe has not run.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `ip` (String) The public address traffic arrives on. Assigned during provisioning, so it is only meaningful once `wait_for_ready` has returned.
- `pending_apply` (Boolean) True while an edit has not reached the data plane yet. The state stays `active` throughout an edit, so this is the only field that moves when rules or backends change.
- `state` (String) `active`, `stopped_dunning` and `deleted` are settled; an `error_*` value means provisioning failed.

<a id="nestedatt--health_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `health_check`

Optional:

- `interval_seconds` (Number) 5 to 300; defaults to 10.
- `path` (String) The path an `http` check requests. Defaults to `/`; ignored for `tcp`.
- `protocol` (String) `tcp` (the default) or `http`.


<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `entry_port` (Number) The port traffic arrives on.
- `protocol` (String) `http` adds an `X-Forwarded-For` header; `tcp` passes the connection through untouched, which is what HTTPS passthrough needs.
- `target_port` (Number) The port on each backend.
